sizing_recommendation.rationale: SMCI is in-portfolio with an active Layer 2 legal/accounting override — bullish chip momentum does not translate to a bullish stance on the held SMCI position; for flat names (NVDA, AMD), this is a late-cycle consensus narrative with no new event catalyst, forward-looking only, warranting no initiation.
overrides: SMCI: portfolio thesis flags 'accumulating legal risk' — bullish sector news is blocked from generating a bullish stance on this name; any strength is a trim opportunity per the existing plan, not an add.

item.reasoning: The WSJ piece confirms the chip melt-up as a widely-held consensus view, which is informationally weak — by the time a trend earns this framing in mainstream financial press, the marginal buyer is already in. There is no new event here (no earnings beat, no supply shock, no policy catalyst), so this scores as thematic/contextual (Layer 1/2, watch tier) rather than actionable. The most important portfolio implication is negative: SMCI is held with a legal-risk override active, and a bullish sector headline against that backdrop is explicitly gated by the framework. The correct posture per the thesis already on file is to trim SMCI into any strength the melt-up narrative provides, not to add. MSFT is held underwater with no near-term catalyst thesis; the sector tailwind is marginal and not incrementally actionable. Confidence is capped at 0.38 due to both the forward-looking-only and low-specificity flags.
